title: Arrosto di tacchino alle erbe

ingredients.text: 400 g petto di tacchino, in un pezzo
ingredients.original_text: 800 g petto di tacchino, in un pezzo

steps: Legare il petto di tacchino con lo spago da cucina.
Massaggiarlo con rosmarino, salvia, origano, curry, sale e pepe.
Scaldare l'olio in un tegame con carota, cipolla, sedano e aglio a pezzi grossi e rosolare la carne su tutti i lati.
Sfumare con il vino bianco.
Cuocere coperto a fuoco basso per circa 45 minuti, oppure in forno a 180 °C coperto con alluminio per circa un'ora.
Lasciar riposare la carne prima di tagliarla a fette.
Frullare le verdure di cottura con un po' di fondo, scaldare la salsa e servirla con l'arrosto.

title: Coniglio alla ligure con olive taggiasche
steps: Tagliare il coniglio a pezzi, eliminare grasso, fegato e reni, sciacquarlo e asciugarlo.
Tritare finemente la cipolla e tritare l'aglio senza anima insieme agli aghi di rosmarino.
Scaldare l'olio con il trito e il coniglio e rosolare la carne su tutti i lati a fuoco basso senza bruciare il soffritto.
Sfumare con il vino rosso alzando la fiamma finché l'alcol è evaporato.
Aggiungere alloro, timo, olive e un mestolo di brodo caldo, coprire e cuocere piano, unendo altro brodo solo se serve.
Dopo circa un'ora, quando la carne si stacca dall'osso, scoprire e far restringere il sugo in eccesso.

title: Cozze alla tarantina
steps: Tieni le cozze in acqua salata per almeno un'ora, poi strofina i gusci ed elimina il bisso.
In una padella rosola uno spicchio d'aglio schiacciato in metà dell'olio, senza farlo scurire.
Aggiungi le cozze e un rametto di prezzemolo, sfuma con il vino e copri finché si aprono.
Filtra il liquido di cottura con un colino fine e tieni da parte le cozze.
In una padella pulita scalda l'olio rimasto con l'aglio a fettine e il peperoncino spezzettato.
Unisci i pelati schiacciandoli con una forchetta, aggiungi il liquido delle cozze e fai restringere a fuoco basso per circa 10 minuti.
Rimetti le cozze nel sugo con il prezzemolo tritato, lascia insaporire qualche minuto e servi con pane abbrustolito.

title: Frittata di zucchine e ricotta al forno
steps: Preriscalda il forno a 180 °C statico.
Lava e asciuga le zucchine, spuntale e tagliale a rondelle sottili.
Sbatti le uova in una ciotola, incorpora ricotta e parmigiano, regola di sale e pepe e unisci le zucchine.
Fodera una piccola tortiera con carta forno (leggermente unta o inumidita), versa il composto e livellalo.
Cuoci 30 minuti in modalità statica, poi altri 5 minuti ventilato finché la superficie è dorata.
Sforna, taglia a fette e servi tiepida o fredda.

title: Insalata di farro con tonno e ceci
steps: Lessa il farro in abbondante acqua salata secondo i tempi della confezione, scolalo e lascialo raffreddare.
Scola e sciacqua i ceci; sgocciola bene il tonno.
Unisci al farro i ceci e il tonno sbriciolato, condisci con olio e un pizzico di sale e mescola.
Taglia in quattro i pomodorini, lava e asciuga la rucola.
Aggiungi pomodorini e rucola al farro, mescola, regola il condimento e servi subito o tieni in frigo fino al momento.

title: Involtini di pollo al forno

ingredients.text: 300 g petto di pollo, a fette sottili
ingredients.original_text: 600 g petto di pollo, a fette sottili

steps: Stendere le fette di pollo su un tagliere.
Coprire ciascuna con una fettina di fontina e una di prosciutto cotto.
Arrotolarle strette su se stesse.
Sbattere leggermente l'uovo con sale e pepe e passarvi gli involtini.
Rotolarli nel pangrattato e sistemarli su carta forno in una teglia, con un filo d'olio.
Cuocere in forno a 180 °C per 25 minuti.

title: Medaglioni di filetto di maiale ai funghi
steps: Rifilare il filetto da grasso e pellicine, tagliarlo a medaglioni spessi almeno 3 cm e tamponarli con carta da cucina.
Sciogliere il burro chiarificato con la salvia in una padella antiaderente e scottare i medaglioni a fuoco alto circa 2 minuti per lato, salando e pepando leggermente.
Sfumare con il vino bianco e far evaporare l'alcol, poi tenere da parte la carne al caldo.
Nella stessa padella cuocere i funghi affettati sottili con la panna, a fuoco basso e coperto.
Regolare di sale, addensare la salsa con l'amido di mais, rimettere i medaglioni a scaldare e servire.

title: Merluzzo alla livornese
steps: Sbuccia l'aglio ed elimina l'anima interna.
Fai dorare l'aglio nell'olio senza bruciarlo, poi toglilo dalla padella.
Adagia i filetti di merluzzo e rosolali circa 5 minuti per lato.
Bagna con il vino bianco e lascia evaporare a fiamma alta.
Aggiungi la passata, i capperi sciacquati e le olive, e cuoci finché il sugo si restringe.
Poco prima di spegnere unisci il prezzemolo tritato fine e una macinata di pepe.

title: Orata al cartoccio

ingredients.original_text: 900 g orata, 2 pesci da circa 450 g

steps: Preriscalda il forno a 180 °C.
Pulisci l'orata incidendo la pancia, eviscerala, squamala raschiando contro il verso delle squame, poi lavala e asciugala.
Affetta l'aglio, la cipolla, le carote e il limone.
Farcisci la pancia del pesce con alloro, aglio, rosmarino, timo e un pizzico di sale.
Adagia l'orata su un foglio di alluminio con carote, cipolla e limone, condisci con olio, sale e pepe e chiudi bene il cartoccio.
Cuoci in forno per circa 40 minuti.
Apri il cartoccio, elimina erbe e verdure aromatiche e servi con un filo d'olio crudo.

title: Pasta e lenticchie
steps: Se usi lenticchie secche, mettile in ammollo circa 2 ore (accorcia la cottura); se in scatola, sciacquale e basta.
Trita finemente sedano, carota e cipolla.
Scalda l'olio in una pentola e fai soffriggere le verdure con rosmarino e aglio per qualche minuto.
Aggiungi la pancetta e le lenticchie, copri con il brodo caldo e cuoci a fuoco basso: circa 25 minuti se ammollate, 50 se secche non ammollate.
Quando le lenticchie sono tenere, unisci la pasta con altro brodo quanto basta a coprirla e cuoci circa 10 minuti mescolando.
Regola di sale e pepe e servi caldo con un filo d'olio a crudo.

title: Pasta tonno e ceci cremosa
steps: Metti a bollire l'acqua salata per la pasta.
In una padella scalda l'olio del tonno insieme all'olio extravergine.
Trita finemente la cipolla e falla appassire nell'olio a fuoco medio.
Unisci i ceci scolati e il tonno sbriciolato; per una salsa più cremosa frulla metà dei ceci con un po' di acqua.
Cuoci la pasta al dente e scolala tenendo da parte un mestolo di acqua di cottura.
Versa la pasta in padella, aggiungi l'acqua di cottura e manteca qualche istante.
Servi con erba cipollina tritata.

title: Pesce spada alla siciliana
steps: Lava e taglia a metà i pomodorini; sbuccia l'aglio e trita il peperoncino se lo usi.
In una padella larga scalda un filo d'olio con aglio, peperoncino, capperi e olive per un paio di minuti.
Unisci i pomodorini con origano, basilico e un pizzico di sale; copri e cuoci 10 minuti.
Adagia le fette di pesce spada sul fondo in un solo strato, copri e cuoci altri 10 minuti.
Scopri, gira il pesce e lascia andare 5 minuti perché il sugo si restringa un po'; servi subito.

title: Petto di pollo alla cacciatora

ingredients.text: 300 g petto di pollo, a pezzi
ingredients.original_text: 600 g petto di pollo, a pezzi

steps: Pulire i funghi e tagliarli a pezzi.
Tagliare il petto di pollo a bocconi piuttosto grandi.
Sbucciare l'aglio togliendo l'anima e affettare lo scalogno.
Scaldare l'olio con aglio e funghi a fuoco basso per circa 10 minuti.
Aggiungere scalogno e pollo, sfumare con il vino e rosolare finché la carne è colorita in modo uniforme.
Unire i pelati schiacciati e le olive, salare e pepare.
Cuocere dolcemente per circa 10 minuti e servire con basilico fresco.

title: Petto di pollo alla pizzaiola light

ingredients.text: 400 g petto di pollo, a fettine
ingredients.original_text: 400 g petto di pollo, a fettine

steps: In una padella larga cuocere la polpa di pomodoro con l'aglio schiacciato, sale, pepe e origano a fuoco basso per 10-15 minuti.
Regolare di sale, allungare con mezzo bicchiere d'acqua e cuocere ancora un paio di minuti.
Adagiare le fettine di pollo nel sugo, coprirle di salsa e spolverare con altro origano.
Cuocere a fuoco medio con il coperchio socchiuso per circa 10 minuti, girando la carne a metà cottura.
A fuoco spento aggiungere, se si vuole, un filo d'olio a crudo e servire con il sugo.

title: Polpo in umido con patate
steps: Pulisci il polpo togliendo occhi, becco e interiora, sciacqualo bene e taglialo a pezzetti.
Affetta sottilmente la cipolla e mettila in una pentola con olio, passata, aglio e il polpo; sala, pepa e mescola.
Copri e cuoci a fuoco basso per 40 minuti senza aggiungere acqua: il polpo cuoce nel suo liquido.
Sbuccia le patate, tagliale a pezzi regolari, sciacquale e uniscile alla pentola.
Prosegui la cottura coperto per altri 20 minuti (fino a 30 in più se il polpo è grande), finché una forchetta lo infilza senza resistenza.
Regola di sale e pepe, completa con prezzemolo fresco e un pizzico di peperoncino e servi caldo con il sugo.

title: Risotto ai gamberi e arancia

ingredients.original_text: 30 g burro, per il soffritto (25 g + 1 noce)

steps: Sguscia i gamberi eliminando testa e carapace.
Rosolali in padella con l'olio e l'aglio finché cambiano colore, poi tienili da parte.
In una casseruola fai appassire lo scalogno tritato nel burro, aggiungi il riso e tostalo 2-3 minuti.
Sfuma con il vino bianco e lascia evaporare.
Porta a cottura aggiungendo il brodo bollente un mestolo alla volta, mescolando spesso (circa 16-18 minuti).
Pochi minuti prima della fine unisci i gamberi e la scorza d'arancia; regola di sale.
Spegni, manteca con il burro freddo, lascia riposare un paio di minuti e servi.

title: Salmone in crosta di pistacchi e mandorle
steps: Preriscalda il forno a 200 °C.
Trita pistacchi e mandorle e mescolali con pangrattato, un pizzico di sale e l'olio fino a ottenere un composto compatto.
Ungi leggermente una pirofila e sistema i tranci di salmone.
Distribuisci la crosta sulla superficie dei tranci premendo bene.
Cuoci in forno per circa 15 minuti, finché la crosta è dorata, e servi.

title: Saltimbocca alla romana
steps: Togliere grasso e nervetti dalle fettine di vitello e salarle appena, il prosciutto è già sapido.
Passare le fettine nella farina in modo uniforme.
Appoggiare su ognuna una fetta di prosciutto e una foglia di salvia, fermando con uno stuzzicadenti.
Sciogliere il burro in padella e dorare le fettine.
Bagnare con il vino bianco e lasciarlo evaporare del tutto.
Coprire e proseguire la cottura per circa 2 minuti, poi servire subito ben caldi.

title: Scaloppine di pollo al limone

ingredients.text: 500 g petto di pollo, a fettine spesse
ingredients.original_text: 500 g petto di pollo, a fettine spesse

steps: Infarinare le fettine di pollo su entrambi i lati, scuotendo l'eccesso.
Scaldare un filo d'olio con il pizzico d'aglio in una padella antiaderente.
Rosolare le scaloppine da entrambi i lati finché sono dorate, poi salarle.
Versare il succo di limone e un bicchiere d'acqua e lasciare restringere finché si forma una salsina cremosa.
Incorporare il miele per smorzare l'acidità e girare di nuovo le fettine nel fondo.
Completare con scorza di limone grattugiata e pepe macinato, far riposare un attimo e servire con prezzemolo e il sughetto.

title: Sovracoscia di tacchino al limone in padella
steps: Eliminare eventuali penne residue e, se si vuole, disossare la sovracoscia con un coltello.
Scaldare l'olio in padella e adagiare la carne con fette e succo di limone, sale, pepe, rosmarino e alloro.
Rosolare a fiamma vivace finché è dorata, poi girarla e dorare l'altro lato.
Sfumare con il vino bianco e far evaporare l'alcol.
Coprire, abbassare al minimo e cuocere circa un'ora, senza aggiungere acqua.
Alzare la fiamma per ridurre i liquidi e caramellare la carne nel suo fondo, girandola.
Lasciar riposare coperto 5-10 minuti prima di servire.

title: Spaghetti alle vongole
steps: Metti le vongole a bagno in acqua fredda con il sale grosso per circa 2 ore, così rilasciano la sabbia.
In una padella ampia scalda l'olio con lo spicchio d'aglio e i gambi di prezzemolo per circa 1 minuto.
Aggiungi le vongole scolate, copri e cuoci a fuoco vivace finché non si aprono tutte.
Filtra e conserva il liquido di cottura, sguscia circa due terzi delle vongole ed elimina aglio e gambi.
Lessa gli spaghetti in acqua salata e scolali 5 minuti prima del tempo indicato, tenendo da parte un po' di acqua di cottura.
Rimetti gli spaghetti in padella con le vongole, il loro liquido filtrato e un po' di acqua di cottura; salta finché il fondo diventa denso e cremoso.
Completa con prezzemolo tritato fine e una macinata di pepe, poi servi subito.

title: Spezzatino di vitello con patate
steps: Pelare carota e cipolla, pulire il sedano e tagliare tutto a pezzi grossolani.
Scaldare l'olio e far appassire le verdure con le erbe aromatiche a fiamma bassa per 20-25 minuti, senza acqua.
Tagliare il vitello a cubi di 3-5 cm, eliminando grasso e cartilagini.
Unire la carne al soffritto e mescolare finché cambia colore su tutti i lati.
Sfumare con il vino rosso a fiamma alta finché evapora del tutto.
Versare il brodo caldo e cuocere a fiamma bassissima per circa un'ora, coprendo se il liquido cala troppo.
Pelare le patate, tagliarle a pezzi di almeno 4 cm e aggiungerle allo spezzatino.
Cuocere ancora circa 20 minuti, finché le patate sono tenere e il sugo è denso.

title: Straccetti di manzo con rucola e pomodorini
steps: Lavare e asciugare la rucola; lavare i pomodorini e tagliarli a metà.
Battere le fettine di manzo per assottigliarle, ridurle a strisce e passarle velocemente nella farina setacciata.
Scaldare l'olio con l'aglio in una padella antiaderente e far dorare gli straccetti a fuoco vivo per 2-3 minuti.
Salare e pepare, unire i pomodorini e saltare per circa un minuto.
Aggiungere metà della rucola, mescolare ancora un minuto e spegnere.
Impiattare su un letto di rucola e pomodorini crudi, adagiare la carne sopra e finire con un filo d'olio e aceto balsamico.

title: Straccetti di manzo con verdure
steps: Tagliare la carne a striscioline e marinarla circa 15 minuti con salsa di soia, un filo d'olio, zenzero, aglio schiacciato e amido di mais.
Ridurre carota e zucchine a bastoncini e il cipollotto a rondelle.
Saltare le verdure in padella con poco olio e un pizzico di sale a fuoco vivace per pochi minuti, lasciandole croccanti.
In un'altra padella con un filo d'olio rosolare gli straccetti per un paio di minuti, mescolando sempre.
Riunire carne e verdure, aggiungere i semi di sesamo e saltare a fuoco alto per 1-2 minuti; servire subito.

title: Tagliata di manzo con rucola e parmigiano
steps: Tirare fuori la carne dal frigo un'ora prima per portarla a temperatura ambiente.
Scaldare bene la griglia e cospargerla di sale grosso.
Cuocere il controfiletto 3 minuti per lato.
Lasciarlo riposare un minuto su un tagliere, poi affettarlo a circa mezzo centimetro e pepare.
Lavare e asciugare la rucola, togliendo i gambi lunghi.
Disporre rucola e fette di carne nel piatto, completare con scaglie di parmigiano e un filo d'olio.

title: Blanc de poulet à la basquaise

ingredients.text: 1 poivron, rouge ou jaune en lanières
ingredients.original_text: 2 poivron, un rouge et un jaune

ingredients.text: 0.5 tranche jambon, de Bayonne en lanières
ingredients.original_text: 1 tranche jambon, de Bayonne en lanières

steps: Ouvrir chaque blanc de poulet en deux dans l'épaisseur pour obtenir de fines escalopes.
Émincer l'oignon et l'ail, épépiner le poivron et le tailler en fines lanières.
Monder la tomate 30 s dans l'eau bouillante, la peler et la concasser ; couper le jambon en lanières.
Saisir oignon, ail et poivron dans l'huile à feu vif environ 8 min, puis les réserver.
Dans la même poêle, dorer les escalopes quelques minutes de chaque côté.
Remettre les légumes, ajouter jambon, tomate et piment d'Espelette, saler, poivrer et mélanger délicatement.
Verser le vin blanc et le faire réduire à gros bouillons 3 min.
Baisser le feu et laisser mijoter environ 15 min en remuant souvent.

title: Blanquette de veau légère

ingredients.text: 115 g champignons, de Paris en boîte égouttés
ingredients.original_text: 115 g champignons, 1 petite boîte de champignons de Paris

ingredients.text: 2 c. à soupe crème fraîche, légère
ingredients.original_text: 2 c. à soupe crème fraîche, légère

steps: Porter une cocotte d'eau à ébullition ; pendant ce temps, éplucher et émincer oignon, échalote et carottes.
Plonger la viande et les légumes dans l'eau bouillante avec le thym, saler, poivrer, couvrir et cuire 30 min.
Égoutter le tout, le remettre dans la cocotte avec les champignons égouttés et faire revenir brièvement.
Incorporer la crème et le jus de citron en mélangeant bien jusqu'à ce que la sauce nappe.
Servir aussitôt, par exemple avec des haricots verts.

title: Blanquette de veau one pot

ingredients.text: 400 g veau, à blanquette (épaule, tendron ou collier)
ingredients.original_text: 800 g veau, à blanquette (épaule, tendron ou collier)

ingredients.text: 125 g champignons, de Paris en quartiers
ingredients.original_text: 250 g champignons, de Paris en quartiers

ingredients.text: 1 c. à soupe huile d'olive, ou 10 g de beurre
ingredients.original_text: 2 c. à soupe huile d'olive, ou 20 g de beurre

steps: Couper le veau en gros morceaux, les carottes en rondelles, les champignons en quartiers ; hacher oignon et ail, et éplucher puis couper la pomme de terre en dés.
Dans une grande cocotte, saisir rapidement le veau dans l'huile sans trop le colorer.
Ajouter oignon et ail, saupoudrer de farine et remuer 1 min.
Ajouter carottes, champignons, pomme de terre, thym et laurier, verser le bouillon chaud, saler légèrement, poivrer et mélanger.
Couvrir et cuire à feu doux 1 h 15 à 1 h 30 en remuant de temps en temps, jusqu'à ce que la viande soit fondante.
Hors du feu, fouetter la crème avec le jaune d'œuf et le jus de citron, puis l'incorporer doucement sans refaire bouillir.
Parsemer de persil et servir.

title: Brandade de morue légère

ingredients.text: 1 c. à soupe yaourt grec, ou fromage blanc / skyr
ingredients.original_text: 2 c. à soupe yaourt grec, ou fromage blanc / skyr

steps: La veille, rincer la morue et la laisser dessaler 24 h au réfrigérateur dans de l'eau froide, en renouvelant l'eau 3 à 4 fois.
Éplucher et couper les pommes de terre, puis les cuire à l'eau bouillante jusqu'à ce qu'elles soient tendres.
Mettre la morue et l'ail écrasé dans de l'eau froide et pocher 8 à 10 minutes à petits frémissements, sans bouillir.
Égoutter la morue, ôter peau et arêtes, puis l'effilocher finement.
Écraser les pommes de terre en ajoutant le lait tiède petit à petit, puis incorporer le yaourt ou le skyr.
Mélanger la morue à la purée en versant l'huile d'olive en filet, puis poivrer et ajouter un peu de muscade.
Réchauffer à feu doux ou 10 minutes au four à 180 °C, puis servir parsemé de persil.

title: Bœuf bourguignon

ingredients.text: 400 g bœuf à braiser, paleron, joue ou macreuse en cubes
ingredients.original_text: 1200 g bœuf à braiser, paleron, joue ou macreuse en cubes

ingredients.text: 0.5 c. à soupe concentré de tomate
ingredients.original_text: 1 c. à soupe concentré de tomate

ingredients.text: 1 c. à soupe persil, frais haché
ingredients.original_text: 3 c. à soupe persil, frais haché

steps: Facultatif : la veille, faire mariner les cubes de bœuf au frais dans le vin avec un peu de carotte, l'ail écrasé et le bouquet garni.
Égoutter la viande en gardant le liquide, l'éponger, saler, poivrer et la fariner légèrement.
Saisir le bœuf par petites quantités à feu vif dans l'huile chaude d'une cocotte, puis réserver.
Dans la cocotte, faire revenir les lardons puis la carotte en rondelles 5 min.
Remettre la viande, saupoudrer du reste de farine, ajouter le concentré de tomate, puis le vin (ou la marinade filtrée), le bouillon et le bouquet garni ; porter à ébullition.
Couvrir et enfourner à 150 °C pendant 2 h 30 à 3 h, en remuant de temps en temps.
Environ 45 min avant la fin, poêler les champignons au beurre ; dans une autre poêle, glacer les oignons grelots avec un peu de beurre, de sucre et d'eau.
Ajouter champignons et oignons dans la cocotte pour les 30 dernières minutes et rectifier l'assaisonnement.
Retirer le bouquet garni, parsemer de persil et servir bien chaud.

title: Cabillaud épicé au four et ses légumes

ingredients.text: 2.5 cl huile d'olive, pour les légumes
ingredients.original_text: 8 cl huile d'olive, pour les légumes

ingredients.text: 1.5 cl huile d'olive, pour le poisson
ingredients.original_text: 5 cl huile d'olive, pour le poisson

steps: Préchauffer le four à 200 °C.
Couper pommes de terre et courgettes en rondelles, l'oignon en dés et le poivron en lanières.
Mélanger ces légumes avec les tomates cerises, l'huile d'olive, le jus de citron, les gousses d'ail pelées et un peu de sel.
Étaler le tout dans un grand plat et rôtir 25 minutes.
Pendant ce temps, mélanger l'huile, le jus de citron, le paprika, le curcuma et le piment d'Espelette, puis en badigeonner les morceaux de cabillaud.
Poser le poisson sur les légumes et prolonger la cuisson de 15 minutes.
Servir parsemé de persil haché, avec des quartiers de citron.

title: Dos de cabillaud à la basquaise

ingredients.text: 240 g dos de cabillaud (2 morceaux de 120 g)
ingredients.original_text: 480 g dos de cabillaud (4 morceaux de 120 g)

steps: Préchauffer le four à 210 °C. Plonger les tomates 30 secondes dans l'eau bouillante pour les peler facilement.
Épépiner les tomates et les couper en dés ; couper le poivron en cubes, émincer l'oignon et hacher l'ail.
Mettre les légumes dans une sauteuse avec un petit verre d'eau, le piment et le bouquet garni, couvrir et laisser compoter à feu doux.
Saler, poivrer, puis retirer le piment et le bouquet garni.
Cuire le riz environ 20 minutes à l'eau bouillante salée, l'égoutter et le garder au chaud.
Étaler la compotée de légumes dans un plat à gratin, poser les morceaux de cabillaud dessus, saler, poivrer et enfourner 10 minutes.
Servir le poisson et sa basquaise avec le riz.

title: Filet mignon de porc à la moutarde

ingredients.text: 1 c. à soupe moutarde de Dijon, fine et forte
ingredients.original_text: 2 c. à soupe moutarde de Dijon, fine et forte

ingredients.text: 0.5 c. à soupe moutarde, à l'ancienne
ingredients.original_text: 1 c. à soupe moutarde, à l'ancienne

steps: Émincer finement l'oignon.
Chauffer beurre et huile dans une sauteuse et saisir le filet mignon sur toutes ses faces.
Faire fondre l'oignon 5 min dans la matière grasse, déglacer au vin blanc et remettre la viande.
Couvrir et cuire 20 min à feu moyen, puis réserver la viande sur une assiette.
Verser la crème dans la sauteuse en raclant les sucs, saler, poivrer et délayer les deux moutardes.
Couper le filet en tranches épaisses, les remettre dans la sauce, napper et laisser mijoter doucement 10 min.

title: Filet mignon moutarde, pommes de terre et brocoli

ingredients.text: 2 pomme de terre, en fines tranches
ingredients.original_text: 1 pomme de terre, en fines tranches

ingredients.text: 2 c. à soupe moutarde, à l'ancienne
ingredients.original_text: 1 c. à soupe moutarde, à l'ancienne

steps: Fouetter moutarde, sirop d'érable, sauce soja et un peu d'huile, enrober le filet mignon et le laisser mariner au frais au moins 30 min.
Préchauffer le four à 190 °C et trancher finement les pommes de terre.
Étaler les pommes de terre dans un plat, assaisonner de sel, poivre, thym et huile, puis enfourner 15 min.
Détailler le brocoli en fleurettes.
Ajouter le filet et le brocoli à côté des pommes de terre, assaisonner et rôtir 25 à 30 min, jusqu'à 63 °C à cœur.
Laisser reposer la viande quelques minutes, la trancher et servir avec les légumes.

title: Moules marinières
steps: Rincer soigneusement les moules et jeter celles qui sont cassées ou qui restent ouvertes quand on les tapote.
Couper le céleri en petits dés, hacher les échalotes et le persil.
Faire fondre le beurre dans une cocotte et y faire suer doucement échalotes et céleri, sans coloration.
Ajouter les moules, le vin blanc, une bonne dose de poivre, le bouquet garni et le persil.
Couvrir et cuire à feu vif 3 à 4 minutes en mélangeant à mi-cuisson, jusqu'à ce que toutes les moules soient ouvertes.
Remuer une dernière fois pour enrober les moules de jus, retirer le bouquet garni et servir aussitôt.

title: Navarin d'agneau léger

ingredients.text: 300 g agneau, collier ou épaule désossé
ingredients.original_text: 600 g agneau, collier ou épaule désossé

ingredients.text: 100 g pomme de terre, à chair ferme
ingredients.original_text: 200 g pomme de terre, à chair ferme

steps: Éplucher et couper carotte, navet et pommes de terre ; émincer poireau et oignon, concasser la tomate et équeuter les haricots. Dégraisser l'agneau.
Saisir l'agneau 5 à 7 min dans l'huile chaude, puis le réserver.
Faire suer l'oignon et l'ail dans la cocotte et, si souhaité, les saupoudrer de farine.
Remettre l'agneau, ajouter bouillon, tomate, carotte, navet, poireau et bouquet garni ; couvrir et laisser frémir 45 min.
Ajouter pommes de terre et haricots verts et cuire encore 15 à 20 min jusqu'à ce qu'ils soient tendres.
Rectifier l'assaisonnement, retirer le bouquet garni et servir en assiettes creuses parsemées de persil.

title: Navarin d'agneau printanier

ingredients.original_text: 375 ml vin blanc, ½ bouteille (rosé selon l'étape)
1 c. à soupe huile d'olive, un filet

ingredients.text: 1 c. à soupe persil, plat ciselé
ingredients.original_text: 2 c. à soupe persil, plat ciselé

steps: Saler et poivrer l'agneau, puis le saisir à feu vif dans l'huile chaude en cocotte, environ 3 min par face.
Ajouter carotte, navet et oignon coupés et les faire revenir 5 min à feu moyen.
Verser le vin, porter à ébullition et laisser réduire d'un tiers.
Ajouter ail, laurier, clous de girofle et thym, couvrir de bouillon, assaisonner et laisser frémir 30 min.
Ajouter les pommes de terre, le céleri et la tomate en morceaux ainsi que les petits pois.
Couvrir et poursuivre la cuisson à petit feu 20 à 30 min, jusqu'à ce que les pommes de terre soient tendres.
Parsemer de persil ciselé et servir.

title: Papillote de cabillaud au fromage et aux poivrons
steps: Préchauffer le four à 180 °C (th. 6).
Laver, épépiner et peler les poivrons, puis les tailler en fines lanières.
Ciseler finement l'estragon et couper le fromage en tranches de 3 mm.
Faire fondre les lanières de poivron dans une poêle chaude avec un peu d'huile d'olive, ajouter l'estragon en fin de cuisson, assaisonner et réserver.
Retirer la peau du cabillaud et couvrir chaque filet de tranches de fromage.
Sur des feuilles de papier cuisson, disposer les poivrons puis un filet de poisson, arroser d'un filet d'huile, assaisonner et fermer hermétiquement les papillotes.
Cuire 10 minutes au four, puis servir les papillotes ouvertes à table.

title: Papillote de cabillaud au gingembre et citron vert

ingredients.text: 1 c. à café miel, ou sirop d'agave
ingredients.original_text: 2 c. à café miel, ou sirop d'agave

steps: Préparer la marinade : mélanger l'ail haché, le zeste et le jus du citron vert, le gingembre râpé, le miel, l'huile d'olive et la sauce soja.
Enrober les pavés de cabillaud de marinade, couvrir et réserver 1 heure au réfrigérateur.
Préchauffer le four à 210 °C. Tailler les carottes en bâtonnets et émincer la courgette et les mange-tout.
Précuire les carottes 10 minutes à l'eau bouillante, puis les mange-tout et la courgette 2 minutes ; égoutter.
Répartir les légumes sur de grandes feuilles de papier cuisson, poser le cabillaud dessus, arroser du reste de marinade et parsemer de coriandre ciselée.
Fermer les papillotes et cuire 20 minutes au four.

title: Pavés de saumon sur lit de lentilles

ingredients.text: 500 g pavé de saumon, en un filet
ingredients.original_text: 1 kg pavé de saumon, en un filet

ingredients.text: 0.5 c. à soupe chapelure, à l'italienne
ingredients.original_text: 1 c. à soupe chapelure, à l'italienne

steps: Piquer l'oignon avec les clous de girofle, puis le mettre dans une casserole d'eau avec les lentilles, le laurier, 1 c. à soupe d'huile, du sel et du poivre.
Laisser frémir environ 25 minutes jusqu'à ce que les lentilles soient tendres, puis égoutter et retirer l'oignon et le laurier.
Dans une poêle, faire suer les échalotes dans le reste de l'huile.
Verser le vin blanc, ajouter le zeste de citron et laisser réduire de moitié.
Ajouter les lentilles, réchauffer 2 minutes, incorporer le basilic, rectifier l'assaisonnement et garder au chaud.
Allumer le gril du four. Déposer le saumon dans un plat, le badigeonner de miel et le parsemer de chapelure.
Passer sous le gril, sur la grille du haut, 5 à 7 minutes selon l'épaisseur.
Découper le saumon en pavés et les servir sur les lentilles.

title: Petit salé aux lentilles

ingredients.text: 125 g petit salé, échine ou épaule
ingredients.original_text: 250 g petit salé, échine ou épaule
350 g saucisse, de Morteau (1 à 2 pièces)

ingredients.text: 0.5 c. à café thym, séché (ou 1 brin frais)
ingredients.original_text: 1 c. à café thym, séché (ou 1 brin frais)

ingredients.text: 1 c. à soupe moutarde, à l'ancienne
ingredients.original_text: 2 c. à soupe moutarde, à l'ancienne

steps: Rincer les lentilles à l'eau froide et les égoutter.
Dans une cocotte, faire revenir l'oignon en dés dans l'huile d'olive.
Ajouter les carottes en dés et l'ail, puis les lentilles, et remuer environ 1 minute.
Déposer le petit salé et la saucisse, verser le bouillon, puis ajouter le laurier, le thym et du poivre.
Couvrir et laisser mijoter 45 minutes à 1 heure, jusqu'à ce que les lentilles soient fondantes et la viande cuite ; ajouter un peu d'eau chaude si nécessaire.
Retirer le laurier et le thym, trancher la saucisse et parsemer de persil.
Servir bien chaud avec la moutarde à l'ancienne.

title: Poulet au vin blanc et à l'estragon, carottes

ingredients.text: 50 g fromage blanc, fromage frais nature 5 % MG
ingredients.original_text: 100 g fromage blanc, fromage frais nature 5 % MG

ingredients.text: 0.5 c. à café huile d'olive, ou huile de colza
ingredients.original_text: 1 c. à café huile d'olive, ou huile de colza

ingredients.text: 1 c. à café beurre, ou margarine allégée
ingredients.original_text: 2 c. à café beurre, ou margarine allégée

steps: Préchauffer le four à 190 °C (170 °C chaleur tournante).
Disposer les blancs de poulet dans un plat à gratin et les saler.
Faire dorer les échalotes émincées dans l'huile, puis les répartir sur le poulet.
Mélanger la majeure partie du bouillon avec le vin et le fromage frais, ajouter l'estragon haché et poivrer.
Verser sur le poulet, couvrir et enfourner 30 à 35 min jusqu'à cuisson complète.
Pendant ce temps, faire revenir les carottes dans le beurre fondu, mouiller avec le reste du bouillon et cuire environ 15 min.
Ajouter le persil aux carottes, assaisonner et servir avec le poulet, décoré d'estragon.

title: Poulet basquaise

ingredients.text: 500 g cuisse de poulet, poulet fermier découpé en morceaux
ingredients.original_text: 1500 g cuisse de poulet, 1 beau poulet fermier découpé en 8 morceaux

ingredients.text: 165 g tomate, Roma pelées et concassées
ingredients.original_text: 500 g tomate, Roma pelées et concassées

steps: Découper le poulet en morceaux en séparant haut et bas de cuisse sans casser les os.
Émincer les oignons, tailler les poivrons en lanières, peler et concasser les tomates.
Faire dorer les morceaux de poulet côté peau d'abord dans un peu d'huile, en les retournant délicatement, puis les réserver.
Dans la graisse de cuisson, faire suer oignons, ail et poivrons avec le thym et le laurier, sans coloration.
Ajouter les tomates et laisser compoter ; quand les légumes rendent leur jus, incorporer les olives.
Poser le poulet sur les légumes, saler, poivrer, couvrir et cuire à feu très doux environ 45 min en vérifiant la cuisson.
Réduire la sauce si elle est trop liquide (ou détendre avec un peu de bouillon si elle est trop sèche), puis servir.

title: Poulet mijoté aux olives

ingredients.text: 600 g cuisse de poulet, poulet en morceaux
ingredients.original_text: 1800 g cuisse de poulet, poulet en morceaux

ingredients.text: 0.5 c. à café herbes de Provence
ingredients.original_text: 1.5 c. à café herbes de Provence

steps: Saler et poivrer les morceaux de poulet, puis les dorer environ 10 min dans une cocotte avec un filet d'huile d'olive.
Retirer le poulet et faire fondre l'oignon et l'ail émincés dans la cocotte.
Remettre le poulet, mouiller avec le vin blanc et un petit verre d'eau, puis ajouter les olives égouttées.
Assaisonner avec les herbes de Provence, sel et poivre, couvrir et laisser mijoter 40 min à feu doux.
Goûter, rectifier l'assaisonnement, prolonger de quelques minutes si besoin et servir.

title: Poulet à l'estragon

ingredients.text: 2 cuisse de poulet, coupées en deux
ingredients.original_text: 4 cuisse de poulet, coupées en deux

steps: Hacher finement l'ail et les échalotes et couper chaque cuisse en deux.
Chauffer l'huile dans une sauteuse, y faire fondre le beurre et dorer le poulet à feu moyen sur toutes les faces.
Ajouter ail, échalotes et estragon, puis déglacer avec le vin blanc.
Saler, poivrer, couvrir et laisser mijoter environ 20 min en remuant de temps en temps.
Retirer le poulet, incorporer la crème à la sauce et chauffer doucement jusqu'aux premiers frémissements.
Remettre le poulet dans la sauce à l'estragon et servir.

title: Rôti de porc au lait et à la moutarde

ingredients.text: 400 g filet mignon de porc, rôti dans le filet
ingredients.original_text: 1200 g filet mignon de porc, rôti dans le filet

ingredients.text: 1.5 c. à soupe moutarde, à l'ancienne
ingredients.original_text: 4 c. à soupe moutarde, à l'ancienne

steps: Préchauffer le four à 150 °C.
Peler et dégermer l'ail, puis le mettre dans une casserole avec le lait, le laurier, la moutarde et le bouillon ; saler, poivrer et mélanger.
Porter à ébullition puis laisser frémir très doucement environ 15 min.
Saisir le rôti à feu vif sur toutes ses faces dans l'huile, dans une cocotte allant au four, puis jeter la graisse.
Verser le lait infusé sur la viande, couvrir et enfourner 1 h 30.
Trancher le rôti et le servir nappé de sauce.

title: Saumon rôti aux lentilles vertes

ingredients.text: 1 bouquet garni (thym, laurier, queues de persil)
ingredients.original_text: 1 bouquet garni (thym, laurier, queues de persil)

ingredients.text: 300 g pavé de saumon (2 pavés de 150 g avec la peau)
ingredients.original_text: 600 g pavé de saumon (4 pavés de 150 g avec la peau)

steps: Éplucher les carottes et les couper en dés ; peler l'ail et l'oignon, puis piquer l'oignon du clou de girofle.
Ficeler les herbes du bouquet garni.
Mettre les lentilles rincées dans une casserole d'eau froide avec les carottes, l'oignon, l'ail, le morceau de lard et le bouquet garni.
Porter à ébullition puis laisser frémir 30 minutes à demi-couvert, en salant à mi-cuisson.
Environ 10 minutes avant la fin, passer les pavés de saumon sous le gril du four, côté peau vers la chaleur.
Égoutter les lentilles en retirant l'oignon et le bouquet garni ; couper le lard en dés et le faire dorer dans la moitié de l'huile.
Ajouter les lentilles au lard, mélanger et garder au chaud.
Retirer la peau du saumon, saler, poivrer, arroser du reste d'huile et servir sur les lentilles.

title: Saumon à l'oseille des frères Troisgros

ingredients.text: 450 g pavé de saumon, frais, à détailler en escalopes
ingredients.original_text: 900 g pavé de saumon, frais, à détailler en escalopes

steps: Ôter les arêtes du saumon à la pince, puis le détailler en fines escalopes d'environ 140 g.
Aplatir légèrement les escalopes entre deux feuilles de papier cuisson huilées pour obtenir une épaisseur régulière.
Effeuiller l'oseille en retirant les tiges et les nervures, la rincer et déchirer les grandes feuilles.
Dans une sauteuse, réunir l'échalote finement hachée, le fumet, le vin et le vermouth, puis réduire jusqu'à obtenir un liquide sirupeux.
Ajouter la crème et laisser frémir jusqu'à ce que la sauce nappe légèrement.
Plonger l'oseille 10 secondes en remuant la sauteuse sans fouetter, puis assaisonner de quelques gouttes de citron et de sel.
Saisir les escalopes salées dans une poêle antiadhésive très chaude, environ 10 secondes par face, en les laissant à peine cuites.
Napper des assiettes chaudes de sauce, poser le saumon dessus et servir immédiatement.

title: Turbot sauce vierge

ingredients.text: 300 g cabillaud, turbot ou autre poisson blanc
ingredients.original_text: 600 g cabillaud, turbot ou autre poisson blanc

ingredients.text: 1.5 tomate, italiennes, épépinées et en dés
ingredients.original_text: 3 tomate, italiennes, épépinées et en dés

steps: Préchauffer le four à 175 °C (350 °F).
Saler et poivrer le poisson et le déposer dans un plat ou sur une plaque couverte de papier cuisson.
Enfourner 10 à 15 minutes selon l'épaisseur des filets.
Pendant ce temps, mélanger les dés de tomate, l'huile d'olive, les câpres, le vinaigre et les herbes, puis saler et poivrer ; ajouter un peu de sucre si les tomates manquent de goût.
Sortir le poisson et le servir aussitôt nappé de sauce vierge, avec du riz ou une purée et un légume.

title: Œufs pochés, épinards et lentilles

ingredients.text: 0.5 c. à soupe gingembre, frais râpé
ingredients.original_text: 1 c. à soupe gingembre, frais râpé

ingredients.text: 1 c. à soupe huile d'olive, ou huile végétale
ingredients.original_text: 2 c. à soupe huile d'olive, ou huile végétale

ingredients.text: 1 tomate, coupée en deux, chair râpée
ingredients.original_text: 2 tomate, coupées en deux, chair râpée

ingredients.text: 0.5 boîte lentilles, en conserve (398 ml), rincées et égouttées
ingredients.original_text: 1 boîte lentilles, en conserve (398 ml), rincées et égouttées

steps: Dans une grande poêle, faire revenir l'oignon, l'ail et le gingembre dans l'huile environ 3 minutes.
Ajouter le garam masala et le curcuma et remuer 30 secondes.
Ajouter la tomate râpée, les lentilles et la moitié des épinards, couvrir et cuire environ 5 minutes jusqu'à ce que les épinards tombent.
Retirer le couvercle, ajouter le reste des épinards, les laisser tomber puis saler et poivrer.
Former des creux dans la préparation et y casser les œufs.
Couvrir et laisser mijoter 5 à 6 minutes, jusqu'à ce que les blancs soient pris.
Parsemer de feta, ajouter un trait de sriracha et servir.

title: Beef bulgogi rice bowls

ingredients.text: 225 g beef steak, sirloin or tenderloin, thinly sliced
ingredients.original_text: 680 g beef steak, sirloin or tenderloin, thinly sliced
150 g pear, Korean or regular (1/2 large)

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp olive oil, or high smoke point oil
ingredients.original_text: 6 tbsp olive oil, or high smoke point oil
310 g rice, medium-grain, raw weight (5 cups steamed)

ingredients.text: 1 clove garlic, thinly sliced, to serve
ingredients.original_text: 3 clove garlic, thinly sliced, to serve

ingredients.text: 5 g bell pepper, shishito, thinly sliced
ingredients.original_text: 15 g bell pepper, shishito (3), thinly sliced

steps: Slice the beef very thinly and put it in a bowl.
Blitz the pear, onion, marinade garlic, ginger, soy sauce, brown sugar, pepper and sesame oil to a smooth purée.
Pour the purée over the beef, add half the spring onion and the carrot, mix and refrigerate at least 1 hour (overnight is best).
Cook the rice.
Heat a cast-iron pan over high heat and sear the beef in batches with a little oil, 1–2 minutes until caramelised, turning once; scrape the pan clean between batches.
Fill bowls with rice and top with the beef, kimchi, sliced raw garlic, shishito and remaining spring onion.
Finish with sesame seeds and serve with ssamjang on the side.

title: Beef rendang

ingredients.text: 4 chili flakes, dried whole chilies, rehydrated
ingredients.original_text: 12 chili flakes, dried whole chilies, rehydrated

ingredients.text: 0.5 tbsp olive oil, or vegetable oil, for the paste
ingredients.original_text: 2 tbsp olive oil, or vegetable oil, for the paste

ingredients.text: 335 g beef stew meat, chuck, 4 cm cubes
ingredients.original_text: 1000 g beef stew meat, chuck, 4 cm cubes

ingredients.text: 1 tsp olive oil, or vegetable oil, for browning
ingredients.original_text: 1 tbsp olive oil, or vegetable oil, for browning

ingredients.text: 1.5 kaffir lime leaves, very finely sliced
ingredients.original_text: 4 kaffir lime leaves, very finely sliced

steps: Blitz the chilies, onion, garlic, sliced lemongrass, galangal, ginger and paste oil in a food processor until very fine.
Heat the browning oil in a heavy pot over high heat and sear the beef in batches; set aside.
Lower the heat to medium-low and fry the spice paste for 2–3 minutes until it darkens.
Return the beef with all the remaining curry ingredients, bring to a simmer and turn down to a very gentle bubble.
Cover and cook for 1 hour 15 minutes, then check the beef.

Uncover, raise the heat to medium and cook for 30–40 minutes, stirring often, until the oil separates and the sauce reduces to a dark paste clinging to the beef (add a splash of water and keep going if the meat isn't tender yet).
Serve with steamed rice.

title: Bibimbap with Korean beef

ingredients.original_text: 250 g rice, short-grain, raw weight (4 cups cooked)

ingredients.text: 125 g beef steak, tenderloin, very finely sliced
ingredients.original_text: 250 g beef steak, tenderloin, very finely sliced

ingredients.text: 1.5 clove garlic, minced, for the beef
ingredients.original_text: 3 clove garlic, minced, for the beef

ingredients.text: 0.5 tbsp soy sauce, for the beef
ingredients.original_text: 1 tbsp soy sauce, for the beef

ingredients.text: 1 tsp sesame oil, for the beef
ingredients.original_text: 2 tsp sesame oil, for the beef

ingredients.text: 1 tsp garlic, minced, for the vegetables
ingredients.original_text: 2 tsp garlic, minced, for the vegetables

ingredients.text: 4 tsp olive oil, or vegetable oil
ingredients.original_text: 8 tsp olive oil, or vegetable oil

ingredients.text: 1 tsp soy sauce, for the vegetables
ingredients.original_text: 1.5 tsp soy sauce, for the vegetables

ingredients.text: 1 tsp soy sauce, for the sauce
ingredients.original_text: 1.5 tsp soy sauce, for the sauce

ingredients.text: 0.5 clove garlic, finely grated, for the sauce
ingredients.original_text: 1 clove garlic, finely grated, for the sauce

ingredients.text: 1.5 tsp sesame oil, for the sauce
ingredients.original_text: 2.5 tsp sesame oil, for the sauce

steps: Stir the gochujang, mirin, rice vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, grated garlic and sesame oil together until the sugar dissolves.
Mix the grated apple, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, honey and sesame oil, add the beef and marinate 30 minutes (or up to overnight).
Soak the dried shiitake in boiling water for 30 minutes, then squeeze dry and slice; cook the rice.
Sauté the shiitake, carrot, zucchini and spinach one after another in a little oil, seasoning each lightly with salt, garlic, soy and sugar.
Blanch the bean sprouts, drain and cool, then dress with sesame oil, a little garlic and the fish sauce.
Drain the beef and sear it in a very hot pan with a little oil for 3–4 minutes; keep warm.
Fry the eggs to your liking.
Fill bowls with warm rice, arrange the vegetables and beef on top, add the egg, sprinkle with sesame seeds and a drizzle of sesame oil, and serve with the sauce to mix in.

title: Cantonese steamed fish with ginger and scallion

ingredients.text: 1 bunch fresh coriander, small, roughly chopped
ingredients.original_text: 1 bunch fresh coriander, small, roughly chopped

ingredients.text: 1.5 tbsp soy sauce, light or seasoned
ingredients.original_text: 1.5 tbsp soy sauce, light or seasoned

ingredients.text: 285 g cod fillet, or other delicate white fish (sea bass, sole, haddock)
ingredients.original_text: 285 g cod fillet, or other delicate white fish (sea bass, sole, haddock)

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp olive oil, or vegetable oil
ingredients.original_text: 2 tbsp olive oil, or vegetable oil

steps: Julienne the spring onions and ginger and roughly chop the coriander; keep about a third aside for topping.
Stir the soy sauce, salt and sugar into 2 tbsp hot water until dissolved.
Bring 2–5 cm of water to a boil in a steamer setup (a wok with a rack and lid works).
Put the rinsed fillet on a heatproof plate, set it in the steamer, cover and steam over medium heat 7–10 minutes (4–5 for thin fillets), until a knife slides easily through the thickest part.
Pour off the liquid on the plate and scatter the reserved aromatics over the fish.
Heat the oil in a small pan, fry the remaining ginger about 1 minute, add the white spring onion for 30 seconds, then the green parts and coriander.
Add the soy mixture, let it bubble about 30 seconds until the greens just wilt, then pour it over the fish and serve with steamed rice.

title: Chicken larb in lettuce cups

ingredients.text: 25 g rice, jasmine or glutinous, uncooked
ingredients.original_text: 45 g rice, jasmine or glutinous, uncooked

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp olive oil, or vegetable oil
ingredients.original_text: 2 tbsp olive oil, or vegetable oil

ingredients.text: 0.5 chili flakes, fresh Thai bird chili, thinly sliced
ingredients.original_text: 1 chili flakes, fresh Thai bird chili, thinly sliced

ingredients.text: 75 g lettuce, butter or bibb leaves
ingredients.original_text: 150 g lettuce, butter or bibb leaves

steps: Toast the raw rice in a dry wok over low heat for about 10 minutes until golden and fragrant, then grind it to a coarse powder.
Heat the oil in the wok over high heat and fry half the shallots until crisp; lift them out and keep the oil in the wok.
Get the wok smoking hot again, add the minced chicken and stir-fry until browned and slightly crispy.
Season with the sugar, fish sauce and lime juice.
Stir in the toasted rice powder, chili, the remaining raw shallots, spring onion, coriander and mint and toss for about a minute.
Taste and balance with salt, chili, fish sauce or lime as needed.
Spoon into lettuce leaves and scatter the crispy shallots on top.

title: Chinese beef and broccoli

ingredients.text: 1.5 tbsp olive oil, or neutral oil
ingredients.original_text: 2 tbsp olive oil, or neutral oil

ingredients.text: 240 g beef steak, fillet, flank or rump, thinly sliced
ingredients.original_text: 360 g beef steak, fillet, flank or rump, thinly sliced

steps: Stir the cornstarch into a little water until smooth, then mix in the sugar, both soy sauces, rice wine, five-spice, sesame oil and pepper.
Slice the beef thinly and toss it with about 1.5 tbsp of the sauce.
Heat the oil in a skillet or wok over high heat, spread the beef out and let it brown undisturbed for about 1 minute.
Toss the beef, add the garlic and ginger and stir-fry until the meat is no longer pink.
Pour in the rest of the sauce plus about 170 ml water and stir quickly.
Once bubbling, add the cooked broccoli, coat it in the sauce and simmer about 1 minute until glossy and thick.
Take off the heat and serve over rice, scattered with sesame seeds.

title: Chinese cashew chicken

ingredients.text: 1.5 tbsp soy sauce, light or all-purpose
ingredients.original_text: 3 tbsp soy sauce, light or all-purpose

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp rice wine, Chinese cooking wine (or mirin)
ingredients.original_text: 1.5 tbsp rice wine, Chinese cooking wine (or mirin)

ingredients.text: 250 g chicken thigh, skinless, boneless, 2.5 cm pieces
ingredients.original_text: 500 g chicken thigh, skinless, boneless, 2.5 cm pieces

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp olive oil, or peanut oil
ingredients.original_text: 2 tbsp olive oil, or peanut oil
75 g onion, in 2 cm pieces (1/2 onion)

ingredients.text: 0.5 bell pepper, green, in 2 cm pieces
ingredients.original_text: 1 bell pepper, green, in 2 cm pieces

steps: Whisk the cornstarch into the soy sauce until smooth, then add the rice wine, oyster sauce, sesame oil and white pepper.
Toss the chicken with about 1 tbsp of the sauce and leave at least 10 minutes.
Heat the oil in a wok over high heat and stir-fry the garlic and onion for about 1 minute.
Add the chicken and cook about 2 minutes, then add the bell pepper for another minute.
Pour in the remaining sauce with about 3 tbsp water and stir about 1 minute until it simmers and thickens.
Toss in the cashews, take off the heat and serve right away with rice.

title: Crispy scallion ginger salmon

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp olive oil, or neutral oil
ingredients.original_text: 4 tbsp olive oil, or neutral oil
450 g salmon fillet, lightly salted (2 fillets)

ingredients.text: 1 pinch sesame oil, a few drops

steps: Heat a frying pan over medium-high heat with half the oil and lay the salmon in skin-side down.
Leave it alone to sear, 4–7 minutes per side depending on thickness, until no raw centre remains; lift it out.
Mix the soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil and salt with about 60 ml water.
Add the remaining oil to the same pan and fry the ginger until crisp, then add the spring onion until wilted.
Pour in the soy mixture, bring to a boil and switch off the heat.
Serve the salmon on rice, spooning the ginger-scallion sauce over it and scattering coriander on top.

title: Cá kho (Vietnamese caramelised braised mackerel)

ingredients.text: 500 g mackerel, whole, cleaned and gutted
ingredients.original_text: 1000 g mackerel, whole, cleaned and gutted

ingredients.text: 30 g galangal, peeled and thinly sliced (or ginger)
ingredients.original_text: 55 g galangal, peeled and thinly sliced (or ginger)

ingredients.text: 150 g tomato, sliced into thin rounds
ingredients.original_text: 300 g tomato, sliced into thin rounds

ingredients.text: 0.5 chili flakes, fresh bird's-eye chili, optional
ingredients.original_text: 1 chili flakes, fresh bird's-eye chili, optional

steps: Cut the mackerel into thick steaks of about 4 cm, discarding the heads; rub with salt, rinse and pat dry.
Melt the sugar with a splash of water in a small pan and let it bubble, then lower the heat and cook until it turns a dark caramel colour.
Take the caramel off the heat and carefully stir in about 140 ml water to make a dark amber braising liquid.
Line a heavy pot with galangal, shallot and most of the tomato, lay the fish on top in one layer and scatter over the rest of the aromatics, tomato and chili.
Add the fish sauce, soy sauce, caramel liquid and black pepper; top up with a little water so the fish is just covered.
Bring to a boil, add the lime juice, then cover and simmer gently for about 1½ hours, basting the fish from time to time (add hot water if it dries out).
Uncover, taste, and keep braising with the lid ajar until only a thin layer of glossy sauce coats the bottom of the pot.
Serve with steamed rice.

title: Dak galbi (spicy chicken stir-fry)

ingredients.text: 335 g chicken thigh, boneless, bite-size pieces
ingredients.original_text: 500 g chicken thigh, boneless, bite-size pieces

ingredients.text: 1.5 tbsp olive oil, or rice bran oil
ingredients.original_text: 2 tbsp olive oil, or rice bran oil

steps: If the rice cakes are pre-packaged, separate them and soak in warm water for 10 minutes.
Stir together the gochujang, rice wine, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar, garlic, ginger, curry powder, grated onion and a little pepper.
Coat the chicken in the marinade and leave at least 30 minutes (up to overnight for more flavour).
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and spread out the sweet potato, carrot, cabbage, perilla and rice cakes, with the chicken on top.
Cook 3–4 minutes, then lower to medium/medium-low and keep cooking 10–15 minutes, stirring often, until the chicken and sweet potato are cooked through (a lid speeds it up).
Serve hot with rice.

title: Filipino chicken adobo

ingredients.text: 450 g chicken thigh, bone-in serving pieces
ingredients.original_text: 900 g chicken thigh, bone-in serving pieces

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp olive oil, or cooking oil
ingredients.original_text: 4 tbsp olive oil, or cooking oil

steps: Crush the garlic in a mortar, then combine with the chicken and soy sauce and marinate for at least 1 hour.
Lift the chicken out, keeping the marinade and garlic separately.
Heat most of the oil in a pot and sear the chicken for about 2 minutes per side; set aside.
Add the rest of the oil and the marinated garlic and fry until it just starts to colour.
Return the chicken with the leftover marinade, peppercorns, bay leaves and about 180 ml water; bring to a boil, cover and simmer for about 30 minutes until tender.
Pour in the vinegar and let it boil for 1 minute without stirring, then stir and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes to reduce.
Season with sugar and salt and serve hot with rice.

title: Goan-style fish curry

ingredients.text: 0.5 tbsp curry powder, medium, for the paste
ingredients.original_text: 1 tbsp curry powder, medium, for the paste

ingredients.text: 0.5 tsp curry powder, medium, for the flour
ingredients.original_text: 1 tsp curry powder, medium, for the flour

ingredients.text: 10 g ginger, peeled and roughly chopped
ingredients.original_text: 15 g ginger, peeled and roughly chopped

ingredients.text: 200 ml coconut milk, unsweetened (or coconut milk-alternative)
ingredients.original_text: 400 ml coconut milk, unsweetened (or coconut milk-alternative)

ingredients.text: 260 g cod fillet, or other white fish fillets
ingredients.original_text: 520 g cod fillet, or other white fish fillets

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp olive oil, or vegetable oil
ingredients.original_text: 2 tbsp olive oil, or vegetable oil

steps: Blend most of the coriander with the ginger, chili, garlic, chopped spring onion, half the lemon juice, the paste curry powder, a pinch of salt and half the coconut milk until smooth.
Cook the paste in a deep pan for a few minutes until fragrant, then add the remaining coconut milk and simmer until slightly thickened.
Rinse the rice and simmer it, covered, in water until tender and the liquid is absorbed; keep covered.
Cut the fish into strips and toss in the flour seasoned with salt and the remaining curry powder.
Shallow-fry the fish in the oil until golden and just cooked through.
Check the sauce seasoning, add the lemon juice to taste, slip in the fish to warm through and serve with the rice, shredded spring onion and remaining coriander.

title: Gyudon (beef and onion rice bowl)

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp olive oil, or neutral oil
ingredients.original_text: 4 tbsp olive oil, or neutral oil

ingredients.text: 225 g beef steak, chuck or ribeye, very thinly sliced
ingredients.original_text: 450 g beef steak, chuck or ribeye, very thinly sliced
250 g rice, short-grain, raw weight (4 cups cooked)

steps: Cook the rice.
Heat half the oil in a pan over medium-high heat and cook the onions about 10 minutes, stirring often, until soft.
Add the beef and sugar and stir until the beef is lightly browned.
Pour in the mirin, soy sauce and dashi and simmer 10–15 minutes until reduced to a thin sauce; taste and adjust.
Meanwhile fry the eggs sunny-side up in another pan with the remaining oil, keeping the yolks runny.
Spoon rice into bowls, pile on the beef and onions with some sauce, top each with an egg and finish with spring onion and sesame seeds.

title: Gà nướng sả (Vietnamese lemongrass grilled chicken)

ingredients.text: 150 g rice, or rice vermicelli, to serve
ingredients.original_text: 300 g rice, or rice vermicelli, to serve

steps: Whisk all the marinade ingredients together in a bowl.
Coat the chicken well and refrigerate for at least 3 hours, ideally overnight.
Heat the grill (or a grill pan) to about 200°C.
Grill the chicken, turning now and then, until charred on both sides and 74°C in the thickest part.
Rest for 5 minutes, then slice.
Serve hot with rice or rice vermicelli.

title: Healthy chicken tikka masala with spinach

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp olive oil, or rapeseed oil
ingredients.original_text: 2 tbsp olive oil, or rapeseed oil

ingredients.text: 2 chicken breast, small, skinless, cut into chunks
ingredients.original_text: 4 chicken breast, small, skinless, cut into chunks

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp garam masala, tikka spice powder
ingredients.original_text: 2 tbsp garam masala, tikka spice powder

ingredients.text: 150 g rice, brown basmati, to serve
ingredients.original_text: 300 g rice, brown basmati, to serve

steps: Blend the onion, garlic and ginger into a smooth paste.
Fry the paste in half the oil over medium heat for about 15 minutes until golden and sweet; scrape it out and wipe the pan.
Brown the chicken in the rest of the oil, then stir in the tikka spice and cayenne.
Add back the onion paste with the tomatoes and about 200 ml water and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes.
Stir in the ground almonds and spinach and cook 10 minutes more.
Season, take off the heat, stir through the yogurt and coriander and serve with brown basmati rice.

title: Kung pao chicken

ingredients.text: 0.5 tsp olive oil, or vegetable oil, for the peanuts
ingredients.original_text: 1 tsp olive oil, or vegetable oil, for the peanuts

ingredients.text: 170 g chicken breast, in 2 cm cubes
ingredients.original_text: 340 g chicken breast, in 2 cm cubes

ingredients.text: 0.5 tsp olive oil, or vegetable oil, for the marinade
ingredients.original_text: 1 tsp olive oil, or vegetable oil, for the marinade

ingredients.text: 1.5 tbsp olive oil, or vegetable oil, for frying
ingredients.original_text: 3 tbsp olive oil, or vegetable oil, for frying

ingredients.text: 1 piece chili flakes, whole dried red chili, deseeded and chopped
ingredients.original_text: 2 piece chili flakes, whole dried red chilies, deseeded and chopped

ingredients.text: 3 spring onion, white parts, in 2 cm pieces
ingredients.original_text: 6 spring onion, white parts, in 2 cm pieces

steps: Toast the peanuts in the small amount of oil over medium heat, stirring nonstop for about 3 minutes; take off the heat, keep stirring a minute more, then let them cool and crisp up.
Toss the chicken cubes with the marinade oil, cornstarch, rice wine, salt and white pepper and leave for 20 minutes.
Combine both soy sauces, the vinegar, sugar, cornstarch and about 1.5 tbsp water in a small bowl.
Get a wok very hot, add two-thirds of the frying oil and sear the chicken until browned and just cooked; lift it out.
Turn the heat down, add the rest of the oil and fry the garlic, ginger, chilies, Sichuan pepper and spring onion until aromatic.
Put the chicken back, turn the heat to high and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Re-stir the sauce, pour it in and toss for about 1 minute until it thickens and coats the chicken.
Fold in the peanuts and serve straight away with rice.

title: Malaysian nasi goreng with chicken, prawns and egg

ingredients.text: 150 g chicken, boneless, diced into 2 cm pieces
ingredients.original_text: 300 g chicken, boneless, diced into 2 cm pieces

ingredients.text: 50 g green beans, trimmed and chopped
ingredients.original_text: 100 g green beans, trimmed and chopped

ingredients.text: 80 g rice, uncooked weight, cooked and cooled (about 1.5 cups cooked)
ingredients.original_text: 160 g rice, uncooked weight, cooked and cooled (about 3 cups cooked)

steps: Stir-fry the nasi goreng paste with the chicken and onion over medium heat for about 6 minutes.
Add the prawns and green beans and cook 5 minutes more.
Tip in the cooked rice and toss until every grain is coated and piping hot.
Divide between two bowls.
Fry the eggs and set one on each bowl; serve with lettuce, cucumber and tomato on the side.

title: Miso salmon with rice and greens

ingredients.text: 60 g frozen peas, sugar snap peas
ingredients.original_text: 60 g frozen peas, sugar snap peas (a handful)

steps: Boil the rice in salted water until tender, then drain.
Whisk the miso, rice vinegar, ginger and garlic with 100 ml water.
Season the salmon and pan-fry it skin-side down until crisp, then turn it over.
Pour the miso sauce into the pan and slide it under a hot grill until the sauce bubbles and reduces.
Meanwhile boil the bok choy, sugar snaps and baby corn briefly until just tender, then drain.
Plate the rice and greens, set the salmon on top, spoon over the sauce and finish with spring onion.

title: Oven tandoori chicken

ingredients.text: 375 g chicken thigh, bone-in skinless (or legs/drumsticks)
ingredients.original_text: 750 g chicken thigh, bone-in skinless (or legs/drumsticks)

ingredients.text: 0.5 tsp chili flakes, Kashmiri chili powder, for the marinade
ingredients.original_text: 1 tsp chili flakes, Kashmiri chili powder, for the marinade

ingredients.text: 0.5 tsp dried fenugreek leaves, kasuri methi
ingredients.original_text: 1 tsp dried fenugreek leaves, kasuri methi

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp olive oil, or mustard oil, for the marinade
ingredients.original_text: 1.5 tbsp olive oil, or mustard oil, for the marinade

ingredients.text: 0.5 tbsp fresh coriander, chopped, to garnish
ingredients.original_text: 1 tbsp fresh coriander, chopped, to garnish

ingredients.text: 0.5 tsp chili flakes, Kashmiri chili powder, for the chili oil
ingredients.original_text: 1 tsp chili flakes, Kashmiri chili powder, for the chili oil

ingredients.text: 0.5 tbsp olive oil, or mustard oil, for the chili oil
ingredients.original_text: 1 tbsp olive oil, or mustard oil, for the chili oil

steps: Mix the yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, ground spices, salt, fenugreek leaves, oil and lemon juice; taste and adjust salt and heat.
Cut 2–3 deep slits into each piece of chicken, coat thoroughly in the marinade and refrigerate for 6 hours or overnight.
Take the chicken out of the fridge 20 minutes before cooking and heat the oven to 240°C.
Stir together the chili powder and oil for the chili oil.
Set an oiled rack over a foil-lined tray, space the chicken out on it and roast for 15 minutes; baste with leftover marinade or chili oil.
Turn the pieces and roast another 12–15 minutes, then brush with chili oil.
Move to the top shelf under the grill for 3–4 minutes until lightly charred; the thickest part should reach 75°C.
Garnish with coriander and serve with onion, cucumber and lemon wedges.

title: Oyakodon (chicken and egg rice bowl)

ingredients.text: 185 g rice, Japanese short-grain, raw weight
ingredients.original_text: 185 g rice, Japanese short-grain, raw weight (3 cups cooked)

steps: Cook the rice.
Slice the chicken on the diagonal into roughly 2.5 cm pieces.
Bring the mirin and sake to a boil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat, then add the dashi, soy sauce and sugar and return to a boil.
Spread the onion over the pan in one layer, lay the chicken on top, cover and bring back to a boil.
Skim off any foam and fat, then simmer over medium heat about 10 minutes until the chicken is cooked.
Drizzle the beaten eggs slowly over everything, cover and cook just until the egg is softly set, shaking the pan now and then.
Scatter over the spring onion, then slide the chicken, egg and some sauce onto bowls of rice.

title: Pad krapow gai (Thai basil chicken with fried egg)

ingredients.text: 4 tbsp olive oil, or neutral oil, for frying the eggs
ingredients.original_text: 2 tbsp olive oil, or neutral oil, for frying the eggs

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp olive oil, or neutral oil, for stir-frying
ingredients.original_text: 1 tbsp olive oil, or neutral oil, for stir-frying

ingredients.text: 30 g fresh basil, Thai holy basil leaves
ingredients.original_text: 15 g fresh basil, Thai holy basil leaves

steps: Fry the eggs in a wok in the frying oil, basting the tops with hot oil instead of flipping, until the edges are crisp; drain and keep aside.
Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces; roughly pound the garlic and chilies in a mortar (or mince them) and pick the basil leaves.
Heat the wok over high heat with the stir-fry oil and toss the garlic and chili for about 20 seconds until fragrant, without letting them burn.
Add the chicken and stir-fry until almost cooked through, adding a tiny splash of water if the pan gets dry.
Season with oyster sauce, light and dark soy sauce and sugar, and keep tossing for about 30 seconds.
Throw in the holy basil, fold it through and take the wok off the heat as soon as it wilts.
Serve over steamed jasmine rice with the fried egg on top.

title: Satay chicken drumsticks with peanut sauce

ingredients.text: 40 ml coconut milk, full-fat, for the marinade
ingredients.original_text: 80 ml coconut milk, full-fat, for the marinade

ingredients.text: 0.5 tbsp curry paste, Thai red, for the marinade
ingredients.original_text: 1 tbsp curry paste, Thai red, for the marinade

ingredients.text: 0.5 tbsp olive oil, or liquid coconut oil
ingredients.original_text: 1 tbsp olive oil, or liquid coconut oil

ingredients.text: 90 ml coconut milk, full-fat, for the sauce
ingredients.original_text: 180 ml coconut milk, full-fat, for the sauce

ingredients.text: 0.5 tbsp curry paste, Thai red, for the sauce
ingredients.original_text: 1 tbsp curry paste, Thai red, for the sauce

steps: Cut three shallow slashes (about 5 mm deep) into the meaty side of each drumstick.
Stir together the marinade ingredients, coat the drumsticks and work the mixture into the cuts; marinate 3 hours or overnight in the fridge (optional but best).
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and set a rack over a foil-lined tray.
Lay the drumsticks on the rack and dab any remaining marinade on top.
Bake for 35 minutes, then switch to the grill on high for 3–5 minutes to char the skin.
Meanwhile whisk all the sauce ingredients in a small pan and simmer on medium-low for about 5 minutes, stirring, until it is pourable but coats a spoon; keep warm.
Serve the drumsticks with jasmine rice and the peanut sauce for dipping.

title: Taiwanese three cup chicken

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp olive oil, or neutral oil
ingredients.original_text: 1.5 tbsp olive oil, or neutral oil

ingredients.text: 300 g chicken thigh, boneless, skinless, 2.5 cm pieces
ingredients.original_text: 600 g chicken thigh, boneless, skinless, 2.5 cm pieces

ingredients.text: 1 piece chili flakes, whole dried red chili
ingredients.original_text: 2 piece chili flakes, whole dried red chilies

ingredients.text: 10 g fresh basil, Thai basil leaves
ingredients.original_text: 20 g fresh basil, Thai basil leaves (1 cup)

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp rice wine, Chinese cooking wine or mijiu
ingredients.original_text: 2 tbsp rice wine, Chinese cooking wine or mijiu

steps: Mix the light and dark soy, sugar and rice wine in a small bowl.
Warm the oil in a non-stick pan over medium-low and sizzle the ginger and chili for about 30 seconds.
Turn the heat to high, add the chicken and cook until the outside turns white though still raw inside; add the garlic and stir 30 seconds.
Pour in the sauce, bring to a bubble, then lower to medium/medium-high for a steady simmer.
Simmer about 5 minutes, stirring, until the chicken is coloured and the sauce has reduced to a thin syrup (add a splash of water if it reduces too fast).
Stir in the sesame oil and basil until the leaves wilt, then serve on rice with all the pan syrup.

title: Teriyaki chicken with rice

ingredients.text: 0.5 tbsp vinegar, white or rice wine
ingredients.original_text: 1 tbsp vinegar, white or rice wine

steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Whisk the soy sauce, sugar, vinegar, half the oil, garlic and ginger together.
Toss the chicken with half of this sauce in a baking dish and roast 20–25 minutes until cooked through and sticky.
Meanwhile cook the rice as the packet directs.
Soften the onion in the remaining oil over medium heat for 5–8 minutes until lightly golden; set aside.
Stir the cornstarch into the rest of the sauce and bubble it in the pan until thick, then return the onion and add the roasted chicken.
Serve on the rice with any juices from the baking dish and the spring onion on top.

title: Thai green curry with chicken

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp olive oil, or vegetable oil
ingredients.original_text: 2 tbsp olive oil, or vegetable oil

ingredients.text: 3 kaffir lime leaves, torn in half
ingredients.original_text: 6 kaffir lime leaves, torn in half

ingredients.text: 175 g chicken thigh, skinless boneless, sliced
ingredients.original_text: 350 g chicken thigh, skinless boneless, sliced

ingredients.text: 5 g fresh basil, Thai basil (about 8 leaves)
ingredients.original_text: 10 g fresh basil, Thai basil (about 16 leaves)

steps: Heat the oil in a heavy pan over medium-high heat.
Fry the green curry paste with the garlic, ginger and lemongrass for 2–3 minutes until most of the moisture has cooked off (keep your face away from the fumes).
Pour in the stock and coconut milk and stir until the paste dissolves.
Season with the fish sauce and sugar, add the lime leaves and bring to a simmer.
Add the chicken, turn the heat down to a gentle bubble and cook for 7 minutes.
Add the eggplant and simmer about 5 minutes until soft; taste and adjust salt and sweetness.
Add the snow peas for 2 minutes, then stir in the basil and lime juice and take off the heat straight away.
Serve over jasmine rice.

title: Brazilian fish stew (moqueca)

ingredients.text: 340 g cod fillet, firm white fish (halibut, sea bass), in 5 cm pieces
ingredients.original_text: 680 g cod fillet, firm white fish (halibut, sea bass), in 5 cm pieces (1-1.5 lb)

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp olive oil, or coconut / palm oil
ingredients.original_text: 2 tbsp olive oil, or coconut / palm oil

ingredients.text: 0.5 chili flakes, fresh jalapeño, finely diced
ingredients.original_text: 0.5 chili flakes, fresh jalapeño, finely diced

ingredients.text: 4 tbsp parsley, or coriander or spring onion, chopped
ingredients.original_text: 8 tbsp parsley, or coriander or spring onion, chopped

steps: Pat the fish dry, cut into large chunks and rub with salt, lime zest and lime juice; set aside.
In a wide pan, sauté the onion in the oil with a pinch of salt until soft.
Add carrot, red pepper, garlic and jalapeño and cook a few minutes more.
Stir in the tomato paste, paprika, cumin and stock, bring to a simmer, add the tomatoes, cover and cook until the carrots are tender.
Pour in the coconut milk and adjust the salt.
Tuck the fish into the sauce and simmer gently, spooning broth over, until just cooked (thick pieces can finish in a 175°C oven).
Add a squeeze of lime, scatter with herbs and serve over rice.

title: Cajun salmon and sweet potato chowder

ingredients.text: 170 g sweet potato, peeled, 2 cm pieces
ingredients.original_text: 340 g sweet potato, peeled, 2 cm pieces

ingredients.text: 225 g salmon fillet, skinless, 2-3 cm chunks
ingredients.original_text: 450 g salmon fillet, skinless, 2-3 cm chunks

ingredients.text: 75 g corn, frozen and thawed or fresh
ingredients.original_text: 150 g corn, frozen and thawed or fresh

steps: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium-high heat, add the carrot, onion and celery, cover and cook about 5 minutes until softened.
Add the bell pepper and Cajun seasoning and cook 2 minutes more.
Add the sweet potato, stock and about 120 ml water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer about 10 minutes until the potato is tender.
Add the salmon and corn and simmer about 3 minutes until the fish is just opaque in the centre.
Turn the heat to low, stir in the half-and-half, basil and salt and warm through for 1 minute.
Take off the heat, stir in the lemon juice and serve.

title: Cajun salmon with sweet potato wedges
steps: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan).
Toss the wedges on a non-stick tray with half the oil, the rosemary and some salt and roast 25-30 minutes until crisp outside and soft inside.
Rub the salmon with a little oil and coat it in the Cajun seasoning.
For the last 10 minutes of the wedges, roast the salmon on a small tray alongside.
Dress the rocket with the remaining oil and the vinegar and serve with the salmon and wedges.

title: Carne asada bowls with chipotle crema

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp lime, juice, for the marinade
ingredients.original_text: 2 tbsp lime, juice, for the marinade

ingredients.text: 1.5 tsp chili flakes, ground chipotle or chili powder
ingredients.original_text: 3 tsp chili flakes, ground chipotle or chili powder

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp fresh coriander, chopped, for the marinade
ingredients.original_text: 4 tbsp fresh coriander, chopped, for the marinade

ingredients.text: 125 g rice, white, cooked (about 2 cups cooked)
ingredients.original_text: 250 g rice, white, cooked (4 cups cooked)

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp fresh coriander, for the rice
ingredients.original_text: 4 tbsp fresh coriander, for the rice

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp lime, juice, for the rice
ingredients.original_text: 4 tbsp lime, juice, for the rice

ingredients.text: 120 ml crème fraîche, crema or sour cream
ingredients.original_text: 240 ml crème fraîche, crema or sour cream

ingredients.text: 1 chili flakes, small chipotle in adobo
ingredients.original_text: 2 chili flakes, small chipotles in adobo

ingredients.text: 0.5 tbsp lime, juice, for the crema
ingredients.original_text: 1 tbsp lime, juice, for the crema

ingredients.text: 150 g tomato, as pico de gallo
ingredients.original_text: 300 g tomato, as pico de gallo (2 cups)
30 g feta, or cotija, crumbled (1/4 cup)

steps: Combine oil, soy sauce, lime juice, cumin, chipotle powder, coriander and garlic in a zip bag.
Add the steak and marinate in the fridge at least 30 minutes (up to 8 hours).
Heat a grill to high, take the steak out of the marinade, salt both sides and grill about 5 minutes per side.
Rest the steak loosely covered for 5-10 minutes, then slice across the grain and dice.
Toss the cooked rice with coriander and lime juice.
Blend the crema, chipotle, garlic, lime and salt until smooth.
Fill bowls with rice, steak, pico de gallo, avocado, jalapeño, radish and cheese, then drizzle with the chipotle crema.

title: Chicken and sweet potato traybake

ingredients.text: 250 g sweet potato, peeled, 2 cm chunks
ingredients.original_text: 500 g sweet potato, peeled, 2 cm chunks

ingredients.text: 1 lemon, half juiced, half in wedges

steps: Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan).
Toss the sweet potato, onion and garlic with the thyme, rosemary, most of the oil and some seasoning, and roast 15 minutes.
Stir, nestle in the chicken, drizzle with the rest of the oil, add the lemon juice and smoked paprika and roast 15 minutes more.
Add the broccoli and most of the stock and roast a final 15-20 minutes, topping up with stock if the tray dries, until the chicken is cooked through.
Squeeze the soft garlic out of its skins over the tray and serve with lemon wedges.

title: Chicken souvlaki with tzatziki

ingredients.text: 350 g chicken breast, skinless, in large cubes
ingredients.original_text: 700 g chicken breast, skinless, in large cubes

steps: Whisk the oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper into a marinade.
Coat the chicken cubes in it and leave in the fridge for 3-4 hours.
Soak wooden skewers in water, then thread on the chicken and brush with the leftover marinade.
Grill for 10-15 minutes, turning now and then, until cooked through.
Warm the pitas on the grill.
Serve the skewers on the pitas with tomato slices and tzatziki.

title: Chicken tinga

ingredients.text: 0.5 tbsp olive oil, or vegetable oil
ingredients.original_text: 2 tbsp olive oil, or vegetable oil

ingredients.text: 1 chili flakes, chipotle pepper in adobo, chopped
ingredients.original_text: 2 chili flakes, chipotle peppers in adobo, chopped

ingredients.text: 140 g chicken breast, cooked and shredded
ingredients.original_text: 420 g chicken breast, cooked and shredded (3 cups)

steps: Heat the oil over medium heat and fry the sliced onion about 3 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook 2 more minutes until fragrant.
Stir in the tomatoes and parsley, reduce the heat and cook 6-7 minutes until the tomatoes break down (add a splash of water if dry).
Add the shredded chicken and chopped chipotle and simmer about 8 minutes so the flavours meld.
Season with salt and pepper, garnish with parsley and serve with rice and salad or on tostadas.

title: Doro wat

ingredients.text: 1 lemon, juiced, to clean the chicken
ingredients.original_text: 2 lemon, juiced, to clean the chicken

ingredients.text: 60 ml olive oil, or vegetable oil
ingredients.original_text: 125 ml olive oil, or vegetable oil

ingredients.text: garam masala, or mekelesha, to taste
ingredients.original_text: garam masala, or mekelesha, to taste

ingredients.text: 150 g rice, or injera, to serve
ingredients.original_text: 300 g rice, or injera, to serve

steps: Rub the chicken with lemon juice, rinse well, season with salt and leave 30 minutes.
Cook the onions in a dry saucepan over medium-low heat, stirring now and then, for at least an hour until deeply caramelised.
Add the oil and keep cooking the onions 15-20 minutes until they turn darker.
Stir in the berbere, garlic, ginger, cardamom and ghee.
Add the chicken, cover and cook 10 minutes, then add about 250 ml water, cover again and cook 30 minutes more.
Meanwhile boil the eggs about 10 minutes, chill in iced water, peel and cut into pieces.
Add the eggs to the stew, season with mekelesha and salt, and serve with rice or injera.

title: Greek baked fish (psari plaki)

ingredients.original_text: 800 g canned tomatoes, whole peeled (28-oz can)

ingredients.text: 0.5 tsp dried oregano, for the sauce
ingredients.original_text: 2 tsp dried oregano, for the sauce

ingredients.text: 1 pinch dried oregano, for the fish
ingredients.original_text: 0.5 tsp dried oregano, for the fish

steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F) with a rack in the middle.
In an oven-safe pan, cook the onion in the olive oil with a pinch of salt until soft and lightly golden.
Stir in the garlic, then the tomatoes, oregano and pepper; crush the tomatoes, bring to a boil and simmer 10-15 minutes.
Dry the fish and season both sides with salt, oregano, paprika and cumin; squeeze half the lemon over it.
Settle the fish into the sauce and spoon some sauce on top.
Bake 15-25 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily; check so it doesn't overcook.
Scatter with parsley and serve with the remaining lemon in wedges, plus bread or rice.

title: Harissa roast salmon with herby grains

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp olive oil, plus a drizzle
ingredients.original_text: 1 tbsp olive oil, plus a drizzle

steps: Simmer the grains in salted water for 20-25 minutes until just tender.
Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan); mix harissa, oil, honey and the juice of half the lemon.
Toss the salmon and tomatoes in the harissa mix in a baking dish and roast 15 minutes.
In a large bowl combine the spring onions, most of the herbs, the rest of the lemon juice and a little oil.
Drop the peas into the grains for the last minute, then drain thoroughly.
Stir the leftover herbs into the yogurt with salt and a splash of water to loosen.
Toss the grains and peas with the spring onion mix, plate, top with salmon and tomatoes and add the yogurt dressing.

title: Healthy cottage pie

ingredients.text: 0.5 tsp dried oregano, Italian herbs or thyme
ingredients.original_text: 1 tsp dried oregano, Italian herbs or thyme

ingredients.text: 100 g butternut squash, peeled and cubed
ingredients.original_text: 300 g butternut squash, peeled and cubed

ingredients.text: 300 g potato, floury, peeled and cubed
ingredients.original_text: 900 g potato, floury, peeled and cubed

ingredients.text: 50 g greek yogurt, or fat-free fromage frais
ingredients.original_text: 150 g greek yogurt, or fat-free fromage frais

steps: Spray a casserole with oil and soften the onion over medium heat.
Add the garlic, carrot, celery, salt, herbs, sugar and bay leaf and cook about 8 minutes.
Add the mince, breaking it up, and cook until well browned.
Stir in the tomato paste, then the balsamic, soy and Worcestershire sauce.
Add the squash and stock, partly cover and simmer 30 minutes; thicken with the cornstarch slaked in a little cold water and remove the bay leaf.
Meanwhile boil the potatoes in salted water about 15 minutes until tender, drain (keeping a splash of the water) and mash with the yogurt or fromage frais.
